headline: High: shared filesystem and broad network/tooling make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; compliance risk is also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests local PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP server; nullclaw can use MCP plus browser, web_fetch, and delegate. That creates a plausible bridge where MinerU output or parsed document text can be fed into nullclaw as instructions. The pair is not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded into nullclaw's MCP or delegate inputs without sanitization
IF nullclaw treats document text from MinerU as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the two agents for untrusted documents
Prefix all MinerU outputs with a fixed data-only wrapper
Add a human review step before nullclaw executes any instruction extracted from MinerU
Use separate workspaces for raw documents and agent prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every transferred field

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, and local files; nullclaw reads and writes workspace files, audit logs, and secrets, and has broad network egress. A shared workspace or file handoff could expose sensitive document contents to nullclaw and then out to external services. The pairwise path is plausible in default tooling, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree
IF MinerU processes documents containing secrets or personal data
IF nullclaw forwards workspace contents to remote APIs or webhooks
mitigations: Separate input and output directories for the two agents
Restrict nullclaw to redacted copies of MinerU outputs
Turn off network egress for nullclaw during document processing
Review and purge shared workspace files after each run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files, use MCP, and run concurrently; nullclaw also modifies git state and has broad network access. If they share a directory or repository, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt state, and the blast radius can include irreversible git history changes. MinerU's write_filesystem is false, but its MCP/API surfaces still make shared-state conflicts plausible enough to warrant high uncertainty escalation.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF nullclaw performs git operations while MinerU writes derived artifacts into that tree
IF concurrent instances are enabled without locking
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Disable git writes in nullclaw for shared projects
Serialize access with a simple file lock
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing agent that can emit extracted text, tables, and OCR; nullclaw has delegate, schedule, and webhook-style actions. If nullclaw consumes MinerU output as authoritative, extraction mistakes can cascade into external actions or persisted records. Because the pair lacks documented verification boundaries, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses MinerU extraction results without a verification step
IF extracted text is routed into scheduling, webhook, or CRM actions
mitigations: Require a checksum or citation for every extracted fact
Insert a manual approval step before any outbound action
Limit nullclaw to draft-only mode for MinerU-derived content
Compare extracted fields against the source document before commit
requires-engineering: add structured validation rules

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is positioned as private/offline document processing, while nullclaw handles secrets, audit logs, webhooks, and broad networked assistant workflows. If regulated documents or personal data move from MinerU into nullclaw's logged, networked environment, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are processed by MinerU and then stored in nullclaw logs or workspace files
IF nullclaw's retention or webhook destinations differ from the source document policy
mitigations: Keep regulated documents out of nullclaw's workspace
Disable or minimize audit logging for sensitive runs
Set explicit retention and deletion windows before processing
Use a local-only deployment path for both agents
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention policy
